pr.title: Start the fix loop from implement, and end a loop implement started
pr.head: db6da800c4d5816fa0f8f6eb6835025c6bea5513

summary: Projector has two background loops that drive a pull request to a clean review. The review loop (start-review-loop) reviews every new head and posts findings as review threads. The fix loop (start-fix-loop) watches the pull requests its conversation created and runs fix-pr on each one that has findings or a merge conflict. The fix loop only runs when someone starts it, so a pull request that implement opened could sit with unanswered findings until the user noticed nothing was fixing them.

This pull request makes implement start the fix loop itself when it hands a pull request over, or append the pull request to the fix loop the conversation already runs. A new setting, fix.auto_start, turns that off. The hand-over now always says whether a fix loop is watching the pull request and, when none is, why.

A fix loop the user starts runs until the user stops it, idling on an empty tracked file. An auto-started loop should not outlive its pull requests, so the fix loop's watcher script gains --exit-when-closed: once every tracked pull request has merged or closed, it prints DONE and exits. The review loop is unchanged, because it already covers every pull request the operator has in the repository.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Tracked file: the file of owner/repo#number lines that is the fix loop's whole scope. The watcher rereads it every pass.
  • Watcher: watch-threads.sh, a polling script that prints one line per piece of outstanding work, such as FINDING or CONFLICT. Each line becomes a notification to the loop.
  • Pass: one cycle of the watcher, querying every tracked pull request once.

cards.title: Turning it off
cards.html: project config get fix.auto_start --default true prints false when .projector.toml sets fix.auto_start = false, at the repository or in ~/.projector.toml. implement then starts no loop. It also starts none on a host that cannot keep a process running after the turn. A subagent never runs the loop; it hands its pull request back to the top-level conversation.

groups.title: The watcher can end itself
groups.kicker: A new flag makes the fix loop's watcher exit once nothing it tracks is open
intro: watch-threads.sh loops forever by default. Under --exit-when-closed, each pass now records two things: whether any tracked pull request answered as open, and whether the pass failed to learn the state of one. A failed GitHub query, a line in the tracked file that is not owner/repo#number, or a number that names no pull request all count as failing to learn. The watch ends only after a pass where nothing was open and nothing failed, so a network blip cannot end it early.
A tracked file that names no pull request at all, such as one whose merged lines were all deleted, also ends the watch.

files.note: Adds the flag, the open and unsure per-pass variables, and the DONE exit after the state file is written.

checks.text: open and unsure are reset at the top of every pass, so set -u never meets them unset and one pass's failure does not carry into the next. Every failure path that continues past a pull request (a failed or empty fetch_pr, a not-found pull request, a failed fetch_reviews) sets unsure=1 first. Checked by reading each branch.

The DONE check runs after the state file is rewritten and before the --once exit, so a --once run with the flag also prints DONE. The skill's pre-start check runs --once without the flag, so it never does.

files.note: Six tests for the flag through the fake gh: all closed, one open, an empty file, a failed query, a malformed line appended after the pre-start check, and a running watch that must exit within 30 seconds. The fake gains FAKE_GH_LATE_LINE, which appends a line to the tracked file on its first call.

groups.title: implement starts the loop, and the loop knows when to stop
groups.kicker: The skill text agents follow when they hand a pull request over and when the watcher exits
intro: implement's hand-over now ends by starting the fix loop on the new pull request, with every layer of a stack in its tracked set and the watcher run with --exit-when-closed. When the conversation already runs a fix loop, it appends the pull request to that loop's tracked file instead of starting a second one. Only the top-level conversation, the one the user talks to, starts or joins a fix loop. A subagent running implement returns its pull request instead, and the top-level conversation treats it as one it opened. The top-level conversation starts none when the setting is off or the host cannot keep a process running.

start-fix-loop learns the two new situations. When the user asks for a loop while an auto-started one is running, it restarts the watcher without the flag, so the loop then lives until the user stops it. On DONE, it checks the state of each pull request the tracked file names, deletes the closed ones, and restarts the watcher while one is open. Otherwise it finishes its subagents and reports that the loop stopped.

files.note: New text at the end of "Hand the work over": the three cases that start no loop, starting or joining the fix loop otherwise, and what the hand-over says about it.
Says only the top-level conversation runs the loop, that a loop implement started ends when its pull requests close, documents the DONE event, and says what to do on it.

checks.text: The watcher announces nothing when a pull request merges; its rows just drop out. So when DONE arrives, the tracked file usually still names the merged pull requests, which is why the loop checks each one's state with gh pr view rather than trusting the file.

groups.kicker: The new setting and the new default behavior
